subject: Survey of which pinned wheels carry another project's compiled code (BACKLOG #2935, ASVS 15.1.4)
method: The population and the pins are those of the readings snapshot named above.
A wheel tagged none-any was downloaded, its sha256 checked against the lock, and its file list read for compiled files. Nothing was installed or run.

For any other wheel, the pinned Linux x86_64 wheel for CPython 3.14 or abi3, and the Windows amd64 one, were downloaded and hash-checked the same way, and their contents listed. Extension modules were searched as bytes for needed-library names and version strings. A wheel for another platform was not read.
A file list cannot show code linked into an extension, so the pinned source distribution was read as well, hash-checked the same way.
The `pyside6-addons` and `pyside6-essentials` wheels were not fetched. Their answers rest on PyPI project metadata.

The `pyside6` and `shiboken6` wheels were fetched on 2026-10-05, hash-checked against the harness lock, and their contents listed. PyPI offers no source distribution for either, so those two answers rest on the wheel file lists alone.
Where an answer could not be established, it is recorded as not established and the wheel is treated as carrying.
Each answer carries the date it was made. A wheel surveyed again later carries its own date.

wheels.evidence: The wheel holds one extension module, `_cffi_backend`, and no bundled library. wheels.name: pyodbc
wheels.evidence_kind: wheel file list and source tree
wheels.evidence: The wheel holds one extension module and no bundled library. The Linux module names `libodbc.so.2` as a needed library and the wheel does not carry it, so the ODBC driver manager is the host's. The source distribution holds pyodbc's own sources only.

wheels.name: pyside6
wheels.evidence: Neither wheel holds a compiled file. Each holds three Python modules (`__init__.py`, `_config.py` and `_git_pyside_version.py`), typing stubs (59 `.pyi` files in the Linux wheel, 60 in the Windows one), a `py.typed` marker and the wheel's own metadata. No file in either starts with the ELF or the Windows executable signature. The wheel carries a platform tag all the same, and its metadata requires `shiboken6`, `PySide6_Essentials` and `PySide6_Addons` at the same version. PyPI offers no source distribution for it, and with no compiled file there is nothing for one to be linked into.

wheels.name: pyside6-addons
wheels.evidence: The wheel was not fetched or listed. Its PyPI description says it includes Qt modules, and PyPI lists the Linux wheel at about 175 MB. The Qt version inside was not read.
wheels.route_reason: It holds compiled Qt modules, among them the web engine, multimedia and PDF modules. The harness imports none of them, but an install puts them on disk. A flaw filed against Qt names Qt, not `pyside6-addons`, so the vulnerability-history reading would not show it.

wheels.name: pyside6-essentials
wheels.evidence: The wheel was not fetched or listed. Its PyPI description says it includes the essential Qt modules, and PyPI lists the Linux wheel at about 80 MB. The Qt version inside was not read.

wheels.name: shiboken6

projects.name: Microsoft Visual C++ runtime libraries (Windows wheel)

wheels.evidence: The Windows wheel holds shiboken's own extension module and library, and beside them ten Microsoft Visual C++ runtime libraries. Eight give file version 14.44.35211.0 in their own version strings: `concrt140.dll`, `msvcp140.dll`, `msvcp140_1.dll`, `msvcp140_2.dll`, `msvcp140_codecvt_ids.dll`, `vccorlib140.dll`, `vcruntime140.dll` and `vcruntime140_1.dll`. Two give 14.24.28127.4: `vcamp140.dll` and `vcomp140.dll`. The Linux wheel holds only shiboken's own extension module and `libshiboken6` library, which name libc, libm, libgcc_s and libstdc++ as needed libraries and bundle none of them. PyPI offers no source distribution for it, so what is compiled into shiboken's own libraries was not read.

wheels.name: uvloop
wheels.evidence_kind: wheel file list and source tree
wheels.evidence: The wheel holds one extension module, `loop`, of about 15 MB, and no bundled library. It names only libc, libpthread and librt as needed libraries and holds libuv's `uv_version_string` symbol. The source distribution carries libuv under `vendor/libuv`, its `include/uv/version.h` gives 1.48.0, and `setup.py` builds that copy unless told to use the system's. PyPI has no Windows wheel for it.
wheels.route_reason: libuv is the event loop's I/O layer, so the socket reads and writes of an engine that runs on `uvloop` go through it. An advisory against libuv names libuv, not `uvloop`, so the vulnerability-history reading would not show it.

wheels.name: websockets
wheels.evidence_kind: wheel file list and source tree
wheels.evidence: The wheel holds one extension module, `speedups`, and no bundled library. The Linux module names only libc and libpthread as needed libraries, and the source distribution holds one C file, the project's own.
